answer: Copying the same citations across 210 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 210 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the beacon index resolves every citation against the summit checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the falcon audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4466 identities would post 4954 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
